input.summary: Limit the Monthly Base Fee minimum commitment to the current 12-month period, allow reduction on 30 days' notice, and true-up any shortfall instead of a penalty.
input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot take an eight-year take-or-pay minimum, so we limited the minimum monthly fee commitment to the then-current twelve-month period, added a 30 days' notice reduction right, and replaced any shortfall charge with a true-up, with Section 10.3.A made subject to that reduction right. Our preferred position is no minimum commitment at all, but this fallback is acceptable.

ops.text: 8.1A Minimum Commitment. Customer's minimum monthly fee commitment (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term, and Customer may reduce such commitment upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I. If Customer's actual usage-based charges for such period are less than the committed amount, Customer shall pay the difference as a true-up, and no penalty or shortfall charge shall apply.

ops.oldText: Customer agrees that, during the Term, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2.
ops.newText: Customer agrees that, during the Term, and subject to Customer's reduction right in Section 8.1A, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2.
